newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BOURSE WILLING TO CHANGE TRADING SYSTEM.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE WILLING TO CHANGE TRADING SYSTEM.

text.p: The Lithuanian Stock Exchange is willing to change its trading system to introduce mulitiple price fixings daily but needs financial aid to do so, a bourse official said Thursday.

"We are willing to change the trading system," Dalia Jasulaityte, director of the trading and settlement department at the stock exchange, told Reuters at a conference on Lithuanian capital markets and investment opportunities.

"When you have a lot of supply and demand and brokers want to act on their accounts and to speculate, maybe we need to have a possibility to do that and that means you need to have several fixings...and maybe continuous trading in the future."
Jasulaityte said the bourse's software does not support multiple price fixings and that it will look to a foreign source to help finance the expensive change.
"We are willing to do it very quickly, but we do not have the financial resources," Jasulaityte said.
"That's why we are looking for some financial aid and it depends on when we get it," Jasulaityte said.
"One of the possibilities is USAID," Jasulaityte said. "This is one that we are in the process of discussing. It seems that they will help, but I don't know what amount they will manage to allocate."
"Now they are revising their budget for the next year and they will definitely make their decision after October," Jasulaityte said.
